**Central Anatolia and Eastern Anatolia** — Konya, Ankara, Kayseri, Erzurum, Sivas. Winter temperatures drop to minus 15-20 degrees. PE becomes brittle under this condition and breaks at the first impact. **TPU or TPE should be preferred.**

**Mediterranean and Aegean coast** — Antalya, Izmir, Muğla. Winter is mild, frost is limited. PE can be used. However, since the summer sun is intense, the UV contribution is important.

**Black Sea** — Humidity is high, temperature is mild. PE can be used, UV resistance is less critical.

**Marmara** — Intermediate region. TPE balanced choice for medium intensity use.

## How to understand the material?

It is difficult to distinguish visually. There are three control methods:

**Product description.** Serious sellers specify the raw material. If not specified, ask.

**Flexibility test.** Tilt the delineator by hand. TPU and TPE offer soft resistance and rise slowly when released. PE feels harder, rebounds quickly, or stays at an angle.

**Cold test.** Leave the sample in the refrigerator for a few hours and bend it. PE hardens significantly under this condition.

## What material are the eco models made of?

The phrase "eco" usually indicates two things: thinner wall thickness or more economical raw materials.

Eco models aren't bad — they reduce cost when used in the right place. In a closed car park, at a limit without the risk of crashing, the eco model stays trouble-free for years.

However, on a main artery, at a point with constant vehicle contact, the eco model incurs renewal costs in a short time. The decision should be made according to the place of use.

trafik-konisi-fiyatlari-2026.title: Traffic Cone Prices 2026 — According to Height, Weight and Reflectivity
trafik-konisi-fiyatlari-2026.summary: Traffic cone price varies depending on height, base weight and number of reflective tapes. In 2026, 50 cm cones are between 330-550 TL, 70-75 cm cones are between 400-1,000 TL, and 90 cm cones are between 730-1,250 TL (excluding VAT). Weight-based models are approximately 30% more expensive than the standard. Public specifications generally require 75 cm and 4 kg weight.
trafik-konisi-fiyatlari-2026.body:
The price range for traffic cones is wide — there can be a threefold difference between two cones of the same size. Knowing where this difference comes from prevents buying products that are too expensive or too cheap to work.

## How much do traffic cones cost?

2026 market ranges (excluding VAT, single):

| Height | Economic | Standard | Weight based |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30–32cm | 180–260 TL | 260–340 TL | — |
| 50cm | 330–420 TL | 420–560 TL | 550–700 TL |
| 70–75cm | 400–620 TL | 620–850 TL | 850–1,050 TL |
| 90cm | 730–900 TL | 900–1.100 TL | 1.100–1.250 TL |

Models with cat eyes and advertising prints are above these ranges. Printed cone sets can exceed 1,000 TL.

## Factors that determine the price

**Length and amount of plastic.** The 90 cm cone contains approximately three times the raw material of the 50 cm cone. This is the main reason for the price difference.

**Body weight.** There are 1.5 kg and 3 kg cones of the same size. The heavier one has a thicker wall thickness, is resistant to impact and blows less in the wind.

**Weight base.** The weight ring made of recycled rubber alone costs 150-300 TL. Weighted models bear this difference.

**Reflective tape.** Glass ball tape is cheap, microprismatic tape is expensive. RA2 class tape costs two to three times as much as RA1.

**Material.** PVC is flexible and unbreakable, PPC is rigid and cheaper. PVC models are generally 20-30% more expensive.

## Is the weighted cone worth the price difference?

It depends. One question for the decision: **is the cone dislodged?**

The weighted model is required when:
- Area open to wind, bridge, open highway
- Heavy vehicle traffic — airflow from a passing truck blows the cone
- Applications where the cone will remain in place for days

The weightless model is sufficient in the following cases:
- Indoor parking lot and interior
- Windless, sheltered areas
- Short-term, supervised applications

The weighted cone also has a disadvantage: it is difficult to carry. A 90 cm weighted cone weighs 8-10 kg, carrying 20 of them is serious business.

## Which cone is required in public specifications?

A common specification in municipal and public procurement is as follows:

- **Height:** 75 cm
- **Weight:** 4 kg
- **Standard:** KGM 2013 Highways Technical Specification Part 503, Type-1
- **Reflective:** dual band, RA2 class
- There may be a corporate logo or printing request

A cone that meets this specification is in the market price range of 700-900 TL. Economical models do not meet this specification — if offered, they would be rejected at the inspection stage.

## Discount rates for bulk purchases

Common levels in the industry:

- 1–24 pieces: list price
- 25–99 pieces: 10–15% discount
- 100–499 pieces: 20–30% discount
- Over 500 units: project price

The advantage of bulk purchasing in cones is higher than in delinators because **cones are nested** and the shipping cost does not increase proportionally.

20 75cm cones hold about three times as much as one — not 20 times as much. This significantly reduces unit shipping costs when purchasing in bulk.

## What to look for in a cheap cone?

**Wall thickness.** The thin body is crushed at the first vehicle pass and does not regain its previous form. Tighten the cone by hand; If it crushes easily, it is thin.

**Tape sticking.** The tape attached only to the surface will be removed in a short time. In quality products, the tape fits into the channel on the body.

**Color quality.** Plastic without UV additives turns pale orange at the end of summer and its visibility decreases.

**Flatness of the base.** The curved base makes the cone unstable and will topple over in light wind.

## Should you rent or buy a cone?

Renting for a few days of use a few times a year may make sense. However, the traffic equipment rental market in Türkiye is limited.

It is always more economical to purchase for continuous or frequent use. The lifespan of a cone is 3-5 years with proper use; During this period, the rental price exceeds the purchase price many times.

trafik-konisi-secimi.title: How to Choose a Traffic Cone? Height, Weight and Reflective Guide
trafik-konisi-secimi.summary: Three criteria are decisive in choosing a traffic cone: height, base weight and number of reflective tapes. 50 cm cone is used in urban works, 75 cm cone is used in main arteries, and 90 cm cone is used in highway and night works. The weight-based model is preferred in windy areas. The number of reflective tapes directly determines the visibility distance.
trafik-konisi-secimi.body:
Choosing a traffic cone is a more technical decision than it seems. If the wrong size is chosen, the driver will notice the cone late; If insufficient weight is chosen, it will topple over at the first wind. This guide explains the three basic criteria and which one is needed in which situation.

## How many cm should the traffic cone be?

The usage area determines the size. 50 cm is sufficient for short-term urban work. 75 cm is required on main arteries and on roads where the speed limit is over 50 km/h. 90 cm cone should be used in highways, night work and places with heavy vehicle traffic.

The logic is simple: as the driver's speed increases, the detection distance becomes longer, and the cone must be visible from further away. Height directly affects visibility.

| Height | Usage area | Typical speed |
|---|---|---|
| 30–50cm | Parking lot, warehouse, short work in the city | 0–30 km/h |
| 70–75cm | Main street, construction site surroundings | 30–70 km/h |
| 90cm | Highway, night work, heavy vehicles | 70+ km/h |

## When do you need a weight based cone?

The weight-based model is used in areas open to wind, on bridges, on roads with heavy vehicle traffic, and in studies where cones will remain in place for a long time. The weight base is usually made of recycled rubber and is threaded into the base of the cone.

A standard 75cm PVC cone weighs approximately 3kg. The weight-based version of the same cone would be 6-7 kg. This difference determines the resistance to the air flow created by the passing vehicle.

There is no need for a weight base for indoor, outdoor or short-term use — it makes transportation difficult and increases cost.

## Why is the number of reflective tapes important?

Reflective tape sends the light from the headlights back to where it came from. As the number of bands increases, the night visibility of the cone increases.

- **Non-reflective**: daytime use only, indoors, warehouse
- **Single reflector**: urban, illuminated roads
- **Double reflective**: night work, unlit road, highway

In the double reflective cone, the lower band is seen from a close distance and the upper band is seen from a far distance. That's why dual band is standard on high-speed roads.

The quality of the reflective material also makes a difference. Bands with microprismatic structures are visible from a greater distance than bands with glass spheres.

## PVC cone or PE cone?

PVC cones are more flexible, regain their shape when hit by a vehicle, and last longer. PE cones are lighter and less costly, but become brittle in the cold.

PVC should be preferred in places that will be used constantly and where vehicle contact is possible. In short-term, controlled areas, PE is sufficient.

## How many cones are needed?

In highway applications, the distance between cones is determined by speed. General rule: leave a distance of half the speed limit in metres. 25 meters at 50 km/h, 45 meters at 90 km/h.

Additional cones are required for the transition zone during lane closure operations. Typically 15-20 cones are used for a 100 meter lane closure.

## What standards must a traffic cone comply with?

In Türkiye, traffic cones are subject to the technical specifications of the General Directorate of Highways. For reflective material, EN 12899 and TS EN 13422 standards are taken as reference. In public tenders, a certificate of compliance with these standards is required.

There is no obligation for private sector use, but non-standard products may cause problems in occupational safety inspections.

ts-en-13422-reflektif-siniflari.title: TS EN 13422 and Reflective Classes - What Does It Mean in the Specification
ts-en-13422-reflektif-siniflari.summary: TS EN 13422 is the European standard for portable traffic warning devices and traffic cones are within this scope. Reflective material is divided into RA1 and RA2 classes according to EN 12899. Class RA2 has a retroreflectivity value of approximately three times that of RA1 and night visibility is significantly higher. In public tenders, RA2 is usually required, in the private sector, RA1 is sufficient in most cases.
ts-en-13422-reflektif-siniflari.body:
The specification says "TS EN 13422+A1 conformity certificate" and "RA2 class reflective". What do these two statements measure, in what situation is it required, what is the consequence of not complying - this article explains them.

## What is TS EN 13422?

TS EN 13422 is the standard covering portable and deformable traffic warning devices. Traffic cones, cylinders and similar temporary marking products are included in this scope.

The standard defines three main things:

**Physical strength.** The product withstands the impact test at a certain speed and continues to function afterwards.

**Rollover resistance.** Staying in place under wind load and air flow during vehicle passage.

**Visibility.** Color coordinates during the day and retroreflective performance at night.

The phrase "+A1" indicates a later change to the standard. If the specification says "+A1", it means compliance with the current version is required.

## What do RA1 and RA2 classes mean?

The performance of the reflective material is measured by the **reflection coefficient**. Its unit is cd/lx/m² — that is, how much of the light coming from a certain angle returns to the source.

EN 12899 standard classifies according to this value:

| Class | Typical structure | Relative brightness | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| RA1 | Glass sphere (microsphere) | Reference | Urban, illuminated road |
| RA2 | Microprismatic | ~3 times RA1 | Highway, unlit road |
| RA3 | High performance prismatic | Above RA2 | Special applications |

The difference means in practice that under the same headlamp illumination, a cone with the RA2 band is noticeable from significantly further away than one with the RA1 band. At high speed, this distance difference is critical to meet the braking distance.

## In what situation is RA2 required?

RA2 is required in the following conditions:

- Roads with a speed limit of 70 km/h and above
- Routes without street lighting
- Night work
- Regions with high risk of fog and rain
- Most public tenders

RA1 is sufficient under the following conditions:

- Illuminated roads in the city
- Parking lot and on-site use
- Daytime applications
- Closed spaces

RA2 material is approximately two to three times more expensive than RA1. Using RA2 where it is not needed puts unnecessary strain on the budget; Using RA1 where necessary is a violation of the specification.

## Does reflective tape lose its performance over time?

Yes. Three factors influence:

**UV exposure.** Sunlight deteriorates the prismatic structure and adhesive over time. Quality tapes maintain their performance for 5-7 years, while cheap ones show a significant decline in 1-2 years.

**Contamination.** Dust and soot directly reduce retroreflection. Regular cleaning restores most of the performance.

**Physical damage.** Scratches and tears damage the prismatic structure. Damaged tape does not reflect in that area.

A simple control method in the field: shine a headlamp at night from a distance of 50 meters. If the tape does not shine clearly, it is time to replace it.

## What happens if a product is purchased without documentation?

There is no legal obligation for private sector use. However, in case of a work accident, the use of non-standard equipment in occupational safety inspection may lead to liability.

Lack of documentation creates direct consequences in public procurement. The inspection and acceptance commission rejects the product, the delivery is not accepted, and the contract may end in termination.

The document comes from the manufacturer, not the seller. Ask your supplier for the product's manufacturer's certificate of conformity.

## What should be taken into consideration when reading the specification?

Traffic cone specifications typically specify:

1. **Height** — 50, 70, 75, 90 cm
2. **Base size and shape** — square, octagon, hexagon
3. **Weight** — body weight and base weight, if any, separately
4. **Material** — PVC, PPC, PE
5. **Number and width of reflective tape** — odd/double, how many mm
6. **Reflective class** — RA1 or RA2
7. **Color** — fluorescent orange, RAL code available
8. **Standard** — TS EN 13422+A1

Deviation in even one of these eight items can eliminate the offer. Mark the specification in pencil and compare it with the product specifications.

If there is uncertainty, you have the right to request written clarification before the tender date — Law No. 4734 defines this.

yol-butonu-kedi-gozu.title: Path Button and Cat's Eye — Types, Mounting and Placement Range
yol-butonu-kedi-gozu.summary: Road button is a reflective marking element embedded or adhered to the asphalt. There are two types: glass ball and lens; The lensed type is visible from 3-5 times further away. It is placed at 6-12 meters intervals at lane separations and 3-6 meters at bends and intersections. The color code indicates direction and lane type: white normal lane, yellow median, red wrong direction, blue fire hydrant.
yol-butonu-kedi-gozu.body:
The road button is a small part, but it does more work than the lane marking when driving at night. In the rain, the paint line disappears, the button remains visible.

## What is a path button?

It is a marking element that is fixed to the asphalt and reflects the light coming from the headlights. It is popularly known as **cat's eye**.

Its body can be cast aluminum, ABS plastic or polycarbonate. The reflector inside has a prismatic structure and sends the light back to the direction it came from.

## Difference between glass ball and lens buttons

There are two technologies and the performance difference is large.

**With glass beads** — small glass beads are present on the surface. It is cheap, has a medium level of reflectivity, and wears out over time.

**Lensed (prismatic)** — has a corner cube shaped prism inside. It sends back light much more efficiently, is visible from 3-5 times farther away than glass beads, and is resistant to abrasion.

The lens type should be preferred on high-speed roads and unlit routes.

## What does the color code mean?

The color of the path buttons is not chosen randomly, it has meaning.

| Color | Meaning |
|---|---|
| White | Normal lane separation |
| Yellow | Median median, opposite direction separation |
| Red | Wrong direction warning, roadside |
| Green | Emergency exit, escape route |
| Blue | Fire hydrant location |

There are also dual-color buttons — appearing white from one direction and red from the other. These warn drivers entering from the wrong direction on one-way roads.

## How to install?

There are three methods:

**Gluing** — fixed to asphalt with epoxy or polyurethane adhesive. It is the fastest method and is sufficient for most applications. The floor must be clean and dry.

**Studed** — holes are drilled for the studs under the button and they are seated together with adhesive. It is preferred in areas where there is a snow plow, the risk of disassembly is low.

**Embedding** — the asphalt is milled and flush with the button surface. It is the most durable method, the snow plow blade does not get stuck on the button. It is the one with the highest workmanship.

Before installation, the floor should be swept and oil and dust should be cleaned. The button stuck to the dirty surface will come off in the first winter.

## How many meters apart should they be placed?

Range varies depending on route and purpose.

| Location | December |
|---|---|
| Straight lane separation | 9–12m |
| Curve and intersection approach | 3–6m |
| Before the pedestrian crossing | 2–3m |
| Median head | 1–2 m |
| Parking lot lane separation | 2–4m |

The rule is this: the more critical the information the driver must perceive, the narrower the range. On a flat road, sparse alignment is sufficient; Tightening the bend in advance indicates a change in direction.

## What is the difference with the ground marking button?

The road button creates a **line** and gives direction and lane information.

Floor marking button (dot button) marks **area** — parking lot boundary, pedestrian area, warning zone. It is usually larger and flatter and can be stepped on.

Sensible surface elements used for the visually impaired are also a separate category: raised dots and lines are designed to be perceived by the cane and foot, their reflective function is secondary.

## How long will it last?

A properly installed road button will last 3-7 years. Three factors determine lifespan:

**Vehicle contact** — buttons on the strip are constantly mashed. Positioning outside the lane, to the edge of the line prolongs life.

**Snow plow** — removes the sticking buttons as the blade passes over the surface. Recessed mounting should be preferred in snow regions.

**Contamination** — soot and dust accumulated on the surface reduces reflectivity. Rain cleans it to some extent, but performance decreases over time in polluted areas.

A night check should be done once a year: If the buttons do not shine clearly when viewed from a distance of 50-100 meters with headlamp light, it is time to replace them.
